brief: Following a two-month sector pullback (SOX down 11% vs SPX up 4%) driven by de-risking, Goldman Sachs sees a more constructive setup heading into 3Q earnings than its cautious 2Q call, with upside to estimates across most semiconductor sub-sectors. SemiCap gets positive estimate revisions from pulled-in WFE spending and long-term visibility into 2028. Compute benefits from an upward bias to hyperscaler capex, lifting server CPUs (rising agentic AI attach) and key ASIC programs. Analog is favored, with a preference for industrial, aerospace/defense and datacenter exposure. Memory/storage has fundamental upside, but GS prefers HDDs and NAND given limited near-term supply additions. Tactical calls: upside for AMAT, STX and MCHP (MCHP a favorite name, with GS arguing the Street under-models the analog recovery); downside for QCOM, KLAC and WDC. Company theses include: AMAT raising margin targets at SEMICON West; STX's HAMR ramp beating WDC; QCOM's datacenter-ramp expectations running ahead of itself; KLAC lagging peers on DRAM-skewed WFE; AMD's Helios ramp lifting 2027 estimates above Street; and ARM facing AGI CPU supply constraints against persistent smartphone royalty weakness.
